title: Deferred features are rejected with generic or wrong diagnostics, not structured unsupported diagnostics
Sized numeric types (i8-i64, u8-u64, f32) are unimplemented and not listed as deferred
Prelude names `Any`, `Eq`, `Hash`, and `Hasher` are unknown
`$.use(mut K)` and other `mut` requirement keys are not implemented
`shape[T]()` and `shape_of(f)` intrinsics are not implemented
Visibility-aware member lookup cannot be exercised: the prototype compiles one module, so every member is visible, and the fixtures need package roles

Embedding simplification cannot be fully exercised: the prototype compiles one module without trait imports or pub fields, so trait availability and the other-module view of a public type are untested, and the fixtures need package roles or pub fields
`type` declarations and local type/impl declarations are rejected as syntax errors
Trait-argument ownership fixtures need the `Iterable` trait or package roles, which the prototype lacks
The parser rejects core grammar forms
`mut fn` closure literals do not parse
Two entry-point reject cases also report `private-type-leak`
Row-kinded generic data arguments such as `Job[$()]` fail to parse
`string.replace` is not implemented
A comma at depth zero does not end a same-line suite
The prototype has no `Iterable` trait, so user `Iterable` impls and `Iterable` bounds fail
`annotate` declarations do not parse, so the fixtures for `[` directly after `annotate` fail
Value embedding is implemented except the variance rule: declared variance markers do not parse (F-705), so an embedded field cannot be shown to be an invariant position
The prototype has no `Iterable` trait, so a type implementing both `Iterable` and `Iterator` cannot be iterated

A member-lookup fixture expects the 03 example's reading of `page.Label.to_string()`, which contradicts the TQ-36 rule (a promoted inherent method beside the receiver's trait method is ambiguous); it needs rewriting with the single-view member rule
Mixed-permission list literal reports `no-common-type` instead of `no-least-common-type`
The `disposed-file` runtime profile named in spec/conformance/README.md does not exist
`string.trim()` removes U+FEFF and keeps U+0085
Optional `?` inside a closure emits WAT that Binaryen cannot parse
A generic function cannot be used as a value, even when its type arguments are known
`pub` on a path-only `use` is accepted
`pub` on a top-level binding is accepted
Declared variance is deferred, so covariant data cannot be written
A backslash before a quote in a raw string is a lexer error
A closure body nested in brackets may hold only one statement, so an indented multi-statement body ending at a comma line fails to parse
The prototype has no pack operations, so `pack.map(` on a local named `pack` resolves as a method call
`annotate` declarations do not parse, so an annotation body holding only an indented `pass` fails
